summary: Nightly scheduled embedding job from customer triggers cascading 5xxs via gateway socket saturation and runtime watchdog resets
description: Issue summary: Between 02:10-02:25 UTC on 2026-03-12, PixelProbe reported a spike in 502/504 responses from the Redwood hosted API for their tenant. Impact: ~45% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx during the window; customer embedding ingestion pipelines stalled and retried, causing downstream batch duplication. Observed pattern: a scheduled bulk embedding job (internal cron) started at 02:00 UTC with high concurrent subrequests, which saturated gateway keepalive sockets and triggered upstream runtime watchdog resets and subsequent 502/504s.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer schedule: submit embedding batch with ~1200 items split across 12 parallel worker threads starting at the same wall-clock time (simulate with test harness)
Ensure each embedding request uses long prompt context (~8k tokens) to exercise KV-prefetch and long-tail GPU memory usage
Run the batch against a dedicated tenant on us-west prod with current autoscaler and kernel-selection heuristic enabled
Observe API gateway metrics (accept queue, keepalive pool), runtime logs (watchdog resets), and downstream 5xx rates
logs: 2026-03-12T02:12:10Z runtime[worker-3]: watchdog: process reset due to long syscall (blocked on CPU fallback path) pid=32481
2026-03-12T02:12:11Z api-gateway[proxy]: upstream 502 returned from runtime-cluster-uswest tenant=pxp-58 request_id=abc123
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Customer reported large synchronous scheduled job; they confirmed a single-nightly cron that fanouts 12 parallel embedding workers.
SRE checked ingress: accept queue and keepalive pool exhausted in us-west frontends during the spike window. Connection churn increased by 8x relative to baseline.

Runtime team found watchdog resets on several worker processes. Core dump traces show thread stalls in the CPU fallback kernels triggered by a recent kernel-selection heuristic change (PR #1280) that aggressively prefers CPU fallback for mixed-length prompts on certain model shapes.

Hypothesis: concurrent long-context embedding requests from a single tenant saturated gateway socket resources (keepalive exhaustion + ephemeral port churn) causing increased latency, which pushed runtime into degraded kernel paths; those CPU fallback paths are single-threaded in current build and block for long syscalls, tripping the watchdog and causing abrupt upstream closure and 502/504 propagation.

Evidence: Watchdog reset traces correlate with the spike in accept_queue_full and a sharp drop in runtime healthy replicas. The recent kernel-selection change was rolled out to 20% of runtime pool in us-west earlier the same week (deploy on 2026-03-10).

Repro attempt in staging: Running a synthetic batch reproduces keepalive exhaustion and triggers 502s when the kernel-selection heuristic is enabled and gateway keepalive_pool_size is at default. Reproduced only when concurrency >=10 and average context length >5k tokens.
Cross-reference: Slack thread #support-pxp (https://slack.redwood/workspace/archives/C07SUP) and PRs: GH-1280, GH-1293 (keepalive tuning experiments).
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported first failures at ~02:11 UTC. They have a nightly ingestion window; asked for immediate mitigation options.

Rafael Ortiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Temporarily bumped frontend keepalive_pool_size for us-west to 1200 and added short-term rate limiting per-tenant to flatten the fanout. Observed 5xx rate drop within 3 minutes.

Lena Park (Runtime) 2026-03-12: Investigating PR #1280 interaction. CPU fallback path is single-threaded and is more likely to be selected for mixed-length sequences; suspecting kernel-selection heuristic amplifies worst-case latency under high concurrent long-context loads.
Customer (PixelProbe) 2026-03-12: Confirmed pipeline resumed after support applied throttle; asking for permanent fix as nightly loads are business-critical.

Rafael Ortiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Filed INT-200421 to roll back kernel-selection heuristic to canary-free baseline for us-west while we patch the CPU fallback implementation. Will coordinate with Runtime team for a staged rollback.

Lena Park (Runtime) 2026-03-13: Patch in progress to make CPU fallback path cooperative (yielding) and to bound concurrent CPU fallbacks per process. Scope includes instrumentation to reject prefetch for extremely long contexts when fallback concurrency is saturated.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied 2026-03-12: increased frontend keepalive_pool_size for us-west, enabled per-tenant burst throttling during nightly windows for PixelProbe, and temporarily rolled back kernel-selection heuristic in us-west (canary nodes). Full remediation: runtime patch to bound CPU-fallback concurrency and make fallback paths yield; autoscaler tuning to warm GPUs earlier for scheduled batches. Plan: deploy runtime fix to staging 2026-03-15, prod rollout in canary ring 2026-03-17 after validation.
notes_for_followup: Add tenant-aware scheduling advisory to account teams and onboard customers doing large nightly batches to use staggered windows
Add a runtime metric for fallback_concurrency and expose it in Ops dashboards
Consider preflight checks in API layer to reject/queue very large bulk imports instead of immediate fanout
Work with customer to de-dupe retry logic in their ingestion pipeline to avoid amplifying the burst
